C-SUPERSEDE-MEMBERSHIP-4-20941257.IntentSummary:
This T2 plan converts the approved `C-SUPERSEDE-MEMBERSHIP-4-20941257` spec into five sequential tasks. It is the replacement B1 slice of the maintainer-directed split of the monolithic `C-SUPERSEDE-MEMBERSHIP-2-C459A20C`; it pays exactly one finding, `F314` (non-exclusive candidate mint acquisition), and it must be independently implementable and verifiable with B2/B3 code absent.
**T-001 — exclusive acquisition and bounded cleanup:** a non-recursive leaf `mkdir` whose `EEXIST` refuses, so losing the existence-check-to-create race writes nothing; a bounded, identity-and-byte-checked cleanup that removes only an invocation-created, invocation-owned leaf and preserves every residue it did not create; the exported self-locking `cleanupCandidate`. **T-002 — candidate-lock cooperation and entry/future-snapshot boundaries:** the tripartite stale-lock reclamation rule, `recordAttempt` snapshot under the lock, the canonical-only future-snapshot WriteEvidence filter, `writePlanNew` live-publisher wait and crash-marker refusal, and `regenerateCursor({apply:true})` entry locking. **T-003 — durable WriteEvidence-audit compatibility seam:** a dedicated exact predicate reached only by `auditWriteEvidenceOutsideScope`, so already-immutable historical WriteEvidence for `.ngrace/changes/active/.candidate-<valid C-ID>.lock` no longer reddens the dynamic archive ratchet, while `isCliLifecyclePath` is never widened and every near miss keeps raising. It is the only task that touches `M-REVIEW` and the only task read against the immutable archive, so it is not folded into T-002. **T-004 — supersede/review transaction safety and complete writer cooperation:** validate-before-fold for every successor/existence/lineage and predecessor/status/archive/replacement class, rollback and cleanup composition, the three-phase review-verdict snapshot, and the candidate-lock cooperation boundary for the whole covered outer-writer population. **T-005 — operational successor identity and close ratchets:** the scope guard re-authored to the replacement id and its byte-invariance base, the `F314` `bundleMinted` pin introduced naming the replacement, and the single staged `F314` `Owner:` line re-homed.
**Payment and record writes.** The plan grammar has no `<Pays>` element: the payment semantics live in this `IntentSummary` and in the spec, are carried structurally by the successor-named `registry.xml` charter row's `<Pays>` child (written by the close's `--flush`), are pinned by the `bundleMinted` fixture in `scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts` (written by T-005), and are stamped as the derived `<PaidBy>` on the retired Finding carrier in `findings-retired.xml` (written by the close's `--retire` after this bundle's archive arrival). `--flush` writes the four live record XML files; an eligible `--retire` writes all seven XML files; neither writer writes `docs/plans/active/RM-GOVERNED-PATH/decisions.md`, so this plan omits it. The exact non-lifecycle source, test, scratch, predecessor-transition, and record paths are enumerated in `ObservedWriteScope`; the close's writes are in the plan because the spec assigns them to the close, not to a task.
**Baselines.** Two bases have distinct roles and must not be conflated. `13e60c68b326e437ccfe6bc2f2090ae4e148da1a` is the approved spec's whole-bundle byte-invariance and scope-guard base: it deliberately predates replacement-spec approval and the committed predecessor transition, so the activated close-time scope guard compares against it and the git-derived predecessor population is two observable active deletions plus three archive arrivals. `f0521c546e2e28f672f4d993b7a8e16802ce52ff` is the clean plan-authoring and implementation starting point: the replacement spec and its approval ledger are committed, the predecessor transition is committed, and a fresh implementation worktree begins here. No task measures against `13e60c6`; only the close-time guard does.
**Gates.** Every task runs its narrow instrument; the full CI-equivalent `bun run validate:ci` is the plan's single `TargetAssertions` `MustPassCommand` and the outer final gate, never a per-task command. The four spec `CloseEvidence` criteria (`AC-NO-UNFORCED-WRITES`, `AC-CLOSE-PAYER`, `AC-CLOSE-LINT`, `AC-CLOSE-TESTS`) are evaluated by the close in the applied-archive state and are deliberately absent from every task's `Satisfies`.
**Known predecessor-plan defects corrected here.** (1) The ignored `.ngrace/scratch/staged-findings.md` is a separately audited transient input, never a git-observable scope-guard allowlist entry. (2) `cleanupCandidate` carries three reachable discriminator classes — nested cleanup; standalone cleanup while another process holds the lock; and the foreign-token/content/identity/`ENOTEMPTY` refusal family — not two. (3) The task that changes `writePlanNew` in `src/grace-generate.ts` authors and runs `src/grace-generate.test.ts`; a cursor-only command is insufficient. (4) The physical predecessor transition is six explicit plan-scope paths, while the git-derived guard population is two active deletions plus three archive arrivals. (5) The superseded predecessor plan was never approved and is provenance only, never a ratified template.

T-001.Title: Exclusive candidate acquisition and bounded cleanup (F314)

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Make candidate acquisition exclusive for both `ngrace spec new` and the implicit mint inside `ngrace supersede`: replace the `existsSync`-then-recursive-`mkdirSync` window in `src/grace-generate.ts` (`writeSpecNew`/`publishSpecNew` and the creation-and-publication transaction the wrappers `mintResolvedBundle`/`mintBundle` share) with a non-recursive leaf `mkdir` whose `EEXIST` refuses. Losing the existence-check-to-create race must write nothing: a competitor's `spec.xml` and any foreign file are preserved byte-for-byte. Pre-existing candidates under both `active/` and `archive/` refuse. Both directions of `AC-MINT-EXCLUSIVE` are driven on isolated fixtures, including the baseline control that reproduces the pre-repair overwrite on a pre-repair copy.

Implement bounded cleanup in `src/grace-generate.ts`: remove a candidate directory only when this invocation created it and it holds no artifact this invocation did not write at the moment of removal; validate before the first delete, so a foreign marker or any failed ownership check leaves `spec.xml`, the marker, and the directory byte-identical with `removed=false`. The exact handled boundary is identity mismatch, changed own bytes, foreign entries, an ordinary removal I/O failure, and `rmdir` `ENOTEMPTY`: each preserves the residue and emits exactly one diagnostic naming the directory. A non-cooperating replacement of this invocation's own file between the byte comparison and the `unlink`, and the uncatchable SIGKILL/power-loss window, are outside the supported model and are not asserted safe. The `AC-CLEANUP-BOUNDED` interleavings (a)–(f) and the repetition/new-timestamp rows are driven with the actual `mkdir`/`rmdir`/`stat` primitives, and `AC-CLEANUP-VALIDATE-FIRST` is driven as a standalone row.

Export `cleanupCandidate` as the self-locking destructive boundary: it acquires the documented reentrant candidate lock itself so no caller can invoke it unlocked, and nested calls reuse the reentrancy depth (`AC-CLEANUP-LOCK-API`). Land the red-first/green test groups in `src/grace-generate.test.ts`; the criterion is met only when both the pre-repair overwrite control reddens and the repaired exclusive-acquisition and cleanup directions green. This task does not touch the fold or membership surfaces.

T-002.Title: Candidate-lock cooperation, attempt snapshot, future-snapshot filter, and entry boundaries

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Implement the tripartite candidate-lock reclamation rule in `src/grace-cursor.ts`: a parseable known-live holder is never stolen for age (wait for release); a parseable known-dead holder is reclaimed immediately; an empty/unparseable/unknown holder waits for `CANDIDATE_LOCK_TTL_MS`; a token-mismatched release is a no-op that preserves the current holder's bytes. Drive `AC-CANDIDATE-RECLAIM-EXCLUSIVE` through the fired seam/barrier: contender B observes the stale token, A reclaims and acquires the replacement lock, then B attempts reclamation from its stale snapshot; assert the callbacks never overlap, A's token and lock bytes survive while A still holds the lock, and B is pending or aborts without removing A's file. Add the mismatched-token no-op control, the own-lock removal control, and the successor-lock preservation control, driven on the real exported boundary with recursive byte snapshots.

Acquire the candidate lock at the approved public entry of `recordAttempt` and snapshot WriteEvidence under it, so a file changed while waiting for a live publisher is included (`AC-ATTEMPT-SNAPSHOT-UNDER-LOCK`). Narrow the **future-snapshot** WriteEvidence filter that `snapshotWriteEvidence` records to the exact canonical engine path `.ngrace/changes/active/.candidate-<valid C-ID>.lock` and keep every near miss visible, each changing exactly one dimension from the valid control id `C-LOCK-EVIDENCE` (`AC-EVIDENCE-FILTER-CANONICAL-ONLY`): the archive-only `.ngrace/changes/archive/.candidate-C-LOCK-EVIDENCE.lock`; the nested-active-only `.ngrace/changes/active/sub/.candidate-C-LOCK-EVIDENCE.lock`; the source-location-only `src/.candidate-C-LOCK-EVIDENCE.lock`; and the other-top-level-only `other/.candidate-C-LOCK-EVIDENCE.lock`. The malformed-id-only control `.ngrace/changes/active/.candidate-not-a-change.lock` is the only row with an invalid `C-*` id. This criterion governs the future snapshot only; the durable read is T-003.

Make `writePlanNew` in `src/grace-generate.ts` wait and revalidate for a live publisher and refuse crash marker residue before its first write, with the two reachable rows of `AC-PLAN-NEW-MARKER-REFUSAL`: (a) a real `ngrace spec new` paused after the `spec.xml` write, where `plan new` stays pending and byte-invariant while the publisher holds the lock, then refuses on the draft-spec prerequisite after release, and a retry after approval creates the plan; (b) an approved `spec.xml` beside a stale marker with no live publisher, refused before any `plan.xml` or ledger write. Make `regenerateCursor({apply:true})` in `src/grace-cursor.ts` acquire at public entry before resolving or reading, driven with the default `allowDirty:false` so the post-lock dirty refusal fires (`AC-REGEN-ENTRY-LOCK`). Because this task changes `writePlanNew` in `src/grace-generate.ts`, it authors and runs the matching `src/grace-generate.test.ts` coverage as well as `src/grace-cursor.test.ts`; the fold-recovery semantics of `foldEpoch`, `recoverCursor`, and `discardAndFoldEpoch` remain B2's and are not asserted here.

T-003.Title: Durable WriteEvidence-audit canonical candidate-lock compatibility seam

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: In `src/review/core.ts`, add a dedicated exact predicate reached only from `auditWriteEvidenceOutsideScope` that filters exactly the canonical engine candidate-lock path `.ngrace/changes/active/.candidate-<valid C-ID>.lock` when that audit reads already-immutable durable historical WriteEvidence. `isCliLifecyclePath` is not modified: its byte-semantics stay restricted to `run.xml`, `run-ledger.xml`, and `run/**`, and its matched-set pin in `src/review/core.test.ts` continues to hold.

Bind both directions of `AC-EVIDENCE-AUDIT-CANONICAL-ONLY`. The filtered control is `.ngrace/changes/active/.candidate-C-LOCK-EVIDENCE.lock`; each candidate-lock near miss changes exactly one dimension with the valid id `C-LOCK-EVIDENCE` held constant and is asserted present in the durable read and therefore a `review.write-evidence-outside-scope` finding: the archive-only `.ngrace/changes/archive/.candidate-C-LOCK-EVIDENCE.lock`; the nested-active-only `.ngrace/changes/active/sub/.candidate-C-LOCK-EVIDENCE.lock`; the source-location-only `src/.candidate-C-LOCK-EVIDENCE.lock`; and the other-top-level-only `other/.candidate-C-LOCK-EVIDENCE.lock`. The malformed-id-only control `.ngrace/changes/active/.candidate-not-a-change.lock` is the only row with an invalid `C-*` id. Labelled separately as non-lock bundle-artifact controls, `.ngrace/changes/active/<C-ID>/spec.xml` and `.ngrace/changes/active/<C-ID>/plan.xml` continue to raise, because the `C-SCOPE-AUDIT-ATTRIBUTION` charter requires the WriteEvidence audit to keep raising on them.

Drive the live archived case: the `review.write-evidence-outside-scope` finding for `.ngrace/changes/active/.candidate-C-SUPERSEDE-MEMBERSHIP-1-7D8B2BE8.lock` is absent while a recursive byte snapshot of `.ngrace/changes/archive/C-SUPERSEDE-MEMBERSHIP-1-7D8B2BE8/` taken before and after the review is identical, proving the repair is reader-side and not an archived-byte edit (`RM-GOVERNED-PATH D41`). The dynamic archive ratchet returns to exactly zero non-lifecycle `.ngrace/` findings **without editing its expected value**, retaining its exact product-pair multiset (`WRITE_EVIDENCE_SCOPE_PRODUCT_RATCHET`); a test that merely changes the ratchet's expected non-lifecycle count from zero to one does not satisfy this criterion. Land the tests in `src/review/core.test.ts`.

T-004.Title: Supersede/review transaction safety and complete outer-writer cooperation

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Establish validate-before-fold in `src/gates/ledger.ts`'s `supersedeChangeBundle` and the explicit/implicit replacement handling moved into the transaction boundary in `src/grace-supersede.ts`: all successor existence/location and lineage validation, and predecessor status/archive/replacement validation, run before `discardAndFoldEpoch` and before every other write. Drive the full `AC-SUPERSEDE-VALIDATE-BEFORE-FOLD` matrix (a)–(h) plus the explicit `--replacement` rows (i) and (j) on disposable projects with recursive SHA-256 snapshots and a direct exit, each leaving the ledger byte-identical and every loose file present. `AC-REFUSE-PRESERVES-CANDIDATES` is driven for a pre-existing target directory and for an explicit `--replacement` target.

Compose rollback and cleanup on every post-mint failure: attempt successor cleanup once, record the outcome always, surface the residual-state diagnostic exactly once only when cleanup preserved residue, and never recurse. Drive the exact `AC-SUPERSEDE-ROLLBACK-CLEANUP` red sequence — spec status write succeeds, plan status write fails, spec rollback write fails persistently — and assert the composition of the original failure with the rollback residue, the single cleanup diagnostic, and the predecessor's last-successfully-written state.

Give `recordReviewVerdict` the approved three-phase snapshot: snapshot bundle location, directory identity, and exact prerequisite `spec.xml`/ledger bytes; evaluate CloseEvidence outside the lock; reacquire and compare all of them before rebuilding from fresh ledger state and writing. Drive the four `AC-REVIEW-VERDICT-THREE-PHASE` cases — spec-byte mutation, ledger-byte mutation, same-path directory replacement with byte-identical prerequisites, and active/archive relocation — each refusing with no verdict/ledger write, plus a clean unchanged prerequisite that writes successfully.

Cover the candidate-lock cooperation boundary for the whole outer-writer population named by `AC-COOPERATING-WRITER-COVERAGE`, including the `pauseCursor`/`resumeCursor` aliases and the `mintResolvedBundle`/`mintBundle` wrappers, with the **three** carved-out reachable discriminators for `cleanupCandidate`: (i) nested cleanup during a handled mint failure, proving reentrant lock use and the validated delete order; (ii) standalone cleanup of a returned, published `AcquiredCandidate` while another process holds that candidate lock, proving it waits, revalidates, and removes only bytes it still owns; and (iii) the foreign-token/content/identity/`ENOTEMPTY` refusal cases of `AC-CLEANUP-BOUNDED`/`AC-CLEANUP-VALIDATE-FIRST`. The fold/recovery writers are covered only at the candidate-lock cooperation boundary; the fold-recovery semantics of `foldEpoch`, `recoverCursor`, and `discardAndFoldEpoch` are B2's and are not asserted here. Land the red-first/green test groups in `src/grace-supersede.test.ts`, `src/gates/core.test.ts`, and `src/grace-generate.test.ts` — the last carrying the `cleanupCandidate`, `mintResolvedBundle`, and `mintBundle` cooperation groups (published-candidate wait/revalidation and wrapper routing), so the criterion is not claimed by the supersede/cursor files alone.

T-005.Title: Operational successor identity, scope guard, and F314 payer pin

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Carry `C-SUPERSEDE-MEMBERSHIP-4-20941257` on the operational identity surfaces named by `AC-SUCCESSOR-ID-DATA`: the successor wrapper and path, the successor plan's assertions and commands, the scope guard identity and activation switch, the payer pins and their tests, and the registry row `name`. Historical predecessor lineage and the exact archived predecessor paths remain permitted history; source/test attribution comments assert the current contract as successor ownership and record a measurement as predecessor history. The relation is made mechanically testable, never a blanket textual absence assertion.

Re-author the activated close-time scope guard in `src/artifact/scope.test.ts` to the replacement identity `NGRACE_SCOPE_GUARD_CHANGE=C-SUPERSEDE-MEMBERSHIP-4-20941257` and byte-invariance base `13e60c68b326e437ccfe6bc2f2090ae4e148da1a`. Its git-derived allowed set is the five forced source files, the seven forced test/ratchet files, the six exact predecessor-transition paths, the seven record XML files, and the bundle's own active and archive arrival — zero globs and no catch-all record-directory prefix, so a planted non-XML file inside `docs/plans/active/RM-GOVERNED-PATH/` reddens. The exact `.ngrace/scratch/staged-findings.md` path is **excluded** from that git-derived allowlist: it is an ignored transient pre-flush input, separately audited, that `git diff` and `git ls-files --others` cannot observe, so it appears in `ObservedWriteScope` and `BaselineAssertions` and in the payment prose but never in the guard's allowed population. The git-derived observable population is exactly two active deletions plus three archive arrivals: the untracked active `plan.xml` is absent from the base commit, so its disappearance is not counted as a git deletion. Drive all six fixtures of `AC-NO-UNFORCED-WRITES`: clean applied archive passes; a forbidden ordinary path reddens; a planted unlisted file inside the governed record directory reddens; unavailable git evidence refuses rather than reporting clean; the exact predecessor transition is allowed; and without activation a later unrelated change of the same kind does not fail.

Introduce the single `F314` `bundleMinted` pin in `scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts` naming `C-SUPERSEDE-MEMBERSHIP-4-20941257` (the clean base has zero `F314` occurrences), and change exactly the single staged `F314` `Owner:` line in `.ngrace/scratch/staged-findings.md` from its measured lineage-1 provenance owner `C-SUPERSEDE-MEMBERSHIP-1-7D8B2BE8` to the replacement id, changing no other staged owner line. The payer ratchet must be red in the applied-archive fixture when the pin is absent or stale and green only when it names the replacement; the test reads the durable XML result the flush produces and never the ignored staged buffer, so a staged-buffer edit alone cannot green it. The payment set remains exactly `{F314}`.
